title: Do nothing, deliberately
standfirst: High desert at three and a half thousand metres, where the first two days are spent doing nothing on purpose.

blocks.heading: Two nights before anything
paras: Leh sits at an altitude where arriving and sightseeing on the same day makes people genuinely unwell.
Two nights doing very little is not lost time; it is what makes the following week possible.

blocks.heading: The Indus valley
blocks.caption: Monastic houses and private estates along the river.
paras: The monasteries along the Indus are the reason most people come, and they are best at the hours when the light is low.
We time the valley by light rather than by distance, which means fewer sites and better ones.

blocks.heading: Beyond the passes
blocks.caption: The high lakes and the Nubra, when the roads allow.
paras: The passes north and east open briefly and the high lakes are at altitudes where sleeping needs care.
We go up for the day and come down to sleep wherever the itinerary allows it.

blocks.heading: Questions members ask
blocks.intro: The ones that come up nearly every time.

a: June to September. Roads over the passes close for much of the rest of the year.
It needs respect rather than fear. We build the acclimatisation in, check daily and adjust the plan rather than the person.
Inner-line permits are required for several areas and take time. We arrange them before dates are fixed.

blocks.heading: We are ready when you are
paras: Every itinerary starts with a conversation about what you actually want from the days, and works backwards to houses, guides and timing from there.
